title: The $1,100 catch-up at 50
hook: Turn 50 this year? You get an extra $1,100 in your Roth.

concepts.title: The catch-up itself
concepts.body: Roth IRA catch-up contributions are $1,100 in 2026. If you turn 50 by December 31, the IRS lets you put in $1,100 extra, on top of the $7,500 base. That total is $8,600 per spouse, per year.

concepts.title: The math, lined up
concepts.body: Base $7,500 + catch-up $1,100 = $8,600 total per year. The catch-up is a flat add-on, not a multiplier. Same Roth account, more dollars in.

concepts.title: Who qualifies (the 50-by-Dec-31 rule)
concepts.body: If you're married, both of you can do it — if you're both 50. The catch-up is a flat add-on per eligible spouse. If you turn 50 by December 31, you qualify for the whole calendar year, even if you turn 50 on December 31.

visual_spec.subtext: You qualify for the full year
